turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_dn_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`, `poscar`
    (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `dn` (the birefringence at
    1064 nm, dimensionless).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict each candidate's birefringence at 1064 nm,
then select the 5 candidates whose birefringence is CLOSEST to 0.1.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I used the training structures mainly by matching structural families and compositions, with extra weight on low-symmetry tetragonal/monoclinic chalcogenide frameworks that had training birefringence near 0.1. The closest structural analogs in the training set were quaternary Cu/Ag/In/Ga/Al selenides and Li–Mg–Ga selenides, plus the Al/Ga–Hg chalcopyrite-like selenides.

Estimated closest candidates:

| rank | candidate | reasoning | estimated dn |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 1 | c071 | Al–Cu–Ge–Se chalcopyrite/stannite-like; interpolates between Ga₂Cu₂Ge₂Se₈ and In₂Cu₂Ge₂Se₈ training examples | ~0.100 |
| 2 | c021 | mixed Al/Ga–Cu–Se/S structure; nearest to Ga₄Ag₄Se₄S₄ training example at 0.104 | ~0.102 |
| 3 | c082 | Al₄Hg₂Se₈, close to Ga₄Hg₂Se₈ and Al₄Hg₂S₈ training analogs | ~0.096 |
| 4 | c096 | Li–Mg–Ga–Se monoclinic framework similar to LiMgGaSe₃ training structures clustered near 0.10 | ~0.098 |
| 5 | c056 | In–Ag–Ge–Se quaternary selenide, close to In₂Cu₂Ge₂Se₈ / In₂Ag₂Sn₂Se₈ analogs | ~0.094 |

Final: c071, c021, c082, c096, c056
